title: Lars Ulrich - Wikipedia
notes: Born 26 December 1963, Gentofte, Denmark; son of the tennis player Torben Ulrich, grandson of Einer Ulrich; Dexter Gordon his godfather. February 1973: taken at nine to Deep Purple in Copenhagen, bought Fireball the next day. First kit a Ludwig from his grandmother at 12 or 13. Moved to Newport Beach, California, in summer 1980 to play tennis; did not make the Corona del Mar High School team. A Y&T show his defining moment; Diamond Head's Lightning to the Nations (1981), to London to see them. An advert in The Recycler; met James Hetfield in 1981 and formed Metallica. 'Known as a pioneer of fast thrash drum beats' (Metal Militia, Fight Fire with Fire, Battery, Damage Inc., Dyers Eve); the double bass in One. From the Black Album a 'less focused and simplified style', the kit from nine pieces to seven. No ride cymbal: he prefers the China ('does not like the "ding"'). Tama Starclassic Maple, 10- and 12-inch rack toms, two 16-inch floor toms, two 22-inch bass drums; signature 14x6.5 steel snare LU1465; Zildjian, Remo, Ahead. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2009, the first Dane; Knight's Cross of the Dannebrog 2017. Inducted Deep Purple in 2016.

title: 'Metallica's Lars Ulrich discusses his "unique" drumming style: "I've never been very interested in ability"', Blabbermouth.net, 20 February 2018
notes: From a Polar Music Prize interview: 'To me, it's always about the song and the band first.' 'What's always the most interesting to me about drumming is how do you fit the drums into what else is going on?' 'I've never been very interested in ability.' 'As much as I grew up on people like Ian Paice from Deep Purple, who obviously has a lot of ability, I also love people like Phil Rudd [AC/DC] and Charlie Watts [The Rolling Stones] ... they make it swing, they make it move.' 'I've always just looked at drums as more of a group instrument.' And from Rhythm (2008): 'I'm not a particularly accomplished drummer but I am very, very, very good at understanding the role of the drums'; 'I spent a lot of time overcompensating for that on the early records.'

title: Joe Taysom, 'The best drummer of all time, according to Lars Ulrich', Far Out, 23 November 2024
notes: On The Howard Stern Show (by video link; the air date not given): asked for the greatest drummer, 'Between Neil and between John — no disrespect — I'll have to go with' John Bonham. The article credits Ian Paice and Phil Rudd among his favourites without quoting him on them.

title: Kill 'Em All - Wikipedia
notes: Released 25 July 1983, Megaforce. Recorded May 1983 with Paul Curcio at Music America Studios, Rochester, New York; Kirk Hammett had replaced Dave Mustaine; Cliff Burton on bass.

title: Ride the Lightning - Wikipedia
notes: Released 27 July 1984, Megaforce. Recorded in three weeks with Flemming Rasmussen at Sweet Silence Studios, Copenhagen.

title: Master of Puppets - Wikipedia
notes: Released 3 March 1986, Elektra. Sweet Silence Studios, Copenhagen, with Flemming Rasmussen; Cliff Burton's last album (he died 27 September 1986).

title: ...And Justice for All (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 7 September 1988, Elektra; Jason Newsted's first full-length album. Recorded over four months in early 1988 with Flemming Rasmussen at One on One Recording Studios, Los Angeles. 'Aggressive complexity, fast tempos, and few verse-chorus structures.'

title: Metallica (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 12 August 1991, Elektra. One on One Recording Studios, Los Angeles, over eight months with Bob Rock. 'A change in the band's music from the thrash metal style of their previous four albums to a slower, heavier, and more refined sound.' Singles: Enter Sandman, The Unforgiven, Nothing Else Matters, Wherever I May Roam, Sad but True.

title: One (Metallica song) - Wikipedia
notes: The third single from ...And Justice for All, written by Hetfield and Ulrich; the video introduced on MTV in January 1989, directed by Michael Salomon, intercut with Johnny Got His Gun.

title: Blackened (song) - Wikipedia
notes: The opening track of ...And Justice for All, written by Hetfield, Ulrich and Jason Newsted, the first Metallica song Newsted is credited with.

title: Live Shit: Binge & Purge - Wikipedia
notes: Box set of 23 November 1993; its Seattle film recorded at the Seattle Coliseum on 29 and 30 August 1989, the Damaged Justice tour.
